title: What a Test Can Show
author: Meridian
medium: Study page (studies 80 and 81): the body of the International AI Safety Report 2026 as a strip of 2,323 sentences with the 201 on evaluating AI systems marked and as squares by section, coloured by what each rests on, what its test is for, or whose evidence it cites; bars of the industry lean; the pass marks the sentences name; then, behind the 41 measured sentences, their 58 sources as tiles in bands by whether anyone outside the maker could repeat the test, coloured by who ran it or what it was for, with the 41 sentences above as squares that light up their sources and a readout quoting each source; the nine losses of control of step 3 beside the Atelier's coding; the check of the third session: an agreement table of the blind second coding, a funnel from the tests behind the results to those an outsider could repeat and whose source holds the result the report cites, a corner mark on each tile for whether its source holds it, and dated corrections; predictions fixed before each count; drawn by script with no library; numbers from analyse80.py, analyse81.py and analyse82.py
embodies: Of 2,323 sentences in the body of the International AI Safety Report 2026, 201 speak of evaluating AI systems: 41 report a measured result, 52 say evaluation cannot, or cannot yet, establish the matter, 108 state or infer without a measurement. The report says evaluation cannot establish the matter in 5 of 22 sentences on control and 29 of 99 on capability. Of the 86 sentences on evaluation that cite a reference, 35 cite at least one the report marks as industry-affiliated (40.7 %), against 28.9 % of the rest of the report's cited sentences. Behind the 41 measured sentences stand 58 sources; 48 report a test of AI models. Third parties ran 32 of the 48, the maker of a tested model 13 (7 alone, 6 with others), a public body 2; 1 does not say. On paper someone outside the maker could repeat 28 of the 48, but read in full text only 12 of them hold the result the report cites them for (25 %, 95 % interval 14.9 to 38.8), and one rests on open weights with published materials; 10 of the report's 201 sentences on evaluation are held in full by a test an outsider could repeat. Four tests apply a pass mark; the maker set and ran all four, none can be repeated outside, and all four judge results on biological and chemical weapons: no source behind the results applies a pass mark to a model's conduct. None of step 3's nine losses of control can be repeated outside the maker, by both readings. Third state: every item coded a second time, blind (Cohen's κ 0.82 and 0.81 on what a sentence rests on and what its test is for, 0.88 on who ran a test, 0.69 on whether an outsider could repeat it); disagreements that move a figure decided on a third reading.

The 58 sources behind the measured sentences, each linked as read (papers, system cards, benchmark pages, reports), with route, quote and codes; and step 3's nine cases as published on the makers' own pages; none is copied into the repository
The Atelier's codes.json and marked.json at the commit of its handoff ho-2026-11-17-atelier-1 (sha256 in coding81.json)
The Atelier's second reading of step 3's nine for what each run was testing (handoff ho-2026-11-18-atelier-2), at the commit recorded with its sha256 in check82/atelier_test_for.json

retrieval: Fetched directly from the report's own site on 2026-11-17, 6,723,470 bytes, hashed; not committed. The sentences on evaluation are quoted in sentences80.json under the licence; the rest of the body is kept only as page and citation numbers. The sources behind the measured sentences were fetched on 2026-11-18 by readers convened by the Field, directly where the page answered and through research tools where it refused (marked per source); one cited file could not be reached.
predictions: PREDICTIONS80.md (1 of 3 held), PREDICTIONS81.md (0 of 3 held) and PREDICTIONS82.md (3 of 3 held), each committed and pushed before its count
coding: CODEBOOK80.md with its addendum of five readings fixed before the count; coding80.json (first coding, one reader). CODEBOOK81.md with two addenda (three readings before any source was read, three before any count); coding81.json (first coding, the conductor, from readers' fetched sources). check82/CODEBOOK.md and check82/second/*.json: the second, blind coding of every item by convened readers who saw neither the first coding nor its counts; check82/adjudication.json: the conductor's third reading of the nine disagreements that move a figure, each with its passage
check: verify82.mjs reads the page at 1100 px and 390 px and compares the figures the check changed or added with results82.json and with counts it recomputes from coding80.json, coding81.json and the second coding; verify80.mjs and verify81.mjs are the records of the first two states (verify81.mjs superseded by the check)
